comment: Composite indexes for Aura.
Slice 1 needed none: every query it made was a single document lookup by id
(users/{uid}, usernames/{name}), and Firestore indexes single fields itself.
Slice 2 adds the first real ones. The friends screen runs two live queries
against `friendships`, both filtered by membership and status and ordered
newest-first. `array-contains` plus an equality plus an orderBy on a third
field is exactly the shape Firestore cannot serve from automatic indexes.
1. accepted friendships for one person   — the friend list
2. pending friendships for one person    — incoming + outgoing requests,
separated client-side on `requestedBy` rather than by a third query,
because one listener over a handful of pending documents is cheaper
than two, and the split is a comparison the client can already make.
Both share the same field shape, so they are one index, not two.
fieldOverrides turns OFF the automatic single-field indexes on the two age
fields. Nothing can query them today — users/{uid} is self-read-only, so a
collection query fails on the first document it would return. The override
exists so that stays true by construction: the day someone widens `list` on
`users` for a leaderboard, `where('isMinor','==',true)` must not be servable
for free. Added after the slice 2 security review flagged it as latent.
Still expected later:
- users:        appearOnLeaderboards ASC, score DESC  (slice 6 leaderboard)
- feed:         createdAt DESC                        (slice 5, subcollection)
- transactions: recipientId ASC, createdAt DESC       (slice 3)
